title: Credit adverse action notice - basics
facts: When a creditor takes adverse action on a credit application, federal law generally requires notice explaining the action and applicable rights.

If adverse action is based in whole or in part on information from a consumer report, the notice must identify the consumer reporting company and explain the consumer's right to obtain a free report and dispute accuracy.
The credit reporting company does not make the lender's decision and generally cannot explain why the creditor denied the application.
Different federal statutes can impose overlapping adverse-action notice requirements.
